wa_goat_wall.blurb: Goat Wall is a huge glacier-carved face above Lost River Road, a few miles up-valley from Mazama in the Methow. It rises about 1,500 feet and stretches more than a mile, with a polished, shattered look to much of the rock. Most of the climbing is long multi-pitch sport from 5.9 to 5.11, with a few trad lines, a single boulder problem and a handful of winter ice routes from WI3 to WI5. Pitch counts run from several to a dozen or more, so expect a full day. The wall is serious, with loose rock and real consequences, and is a poor choice for a first multi-pitch outing without an expert partner or guide.

wa_8_the_ledge.blurb: The Ledge sits high on Burge Mountain above Tonasket in the north Okanogan, on gneiss. It is a low-angled slab and face with bolted lines, and it asks for the longest walk-in of any sector at Burge, which is rewarded by the best easy climbing on the mountain. Most of the routes are sport, and the bulk of them are gentle, in the low 5th-class range up to 5.5, ideal for newer leaders and slab practice. There are also a few harder lines from 5.10 to 5.12. The cliff has good exposure, and loose debris on the ledges around it makes a helmet a smart idea.

wa_foodbar_wall.blurb: Foodbar Wall is a short trad-leaning wall in the Inner Walls canyon above the town of Index in the Skykomish Valley, on the west side next to a cave feature. Nearly everything here is gear climbing, with two sport lines, and all of it falls between 5.10 and 5.11. Several routes have been cleaned and given new bolts in recent restoration work, which makes a few of the easier ones friendly warm-ups, while others keep a bold, gear-only feel. It suits climbers comfortable leading 5.10 who want a quieter alternative to the busier Index walls.

wa_jungle_jim_wall.blurb: Jungle Jim Wall is part of the Orange Wall group on Mt. Erie, on Fidalgo Island in the Northwest. The face runs from moderate angles to overhanging and mixes bolted lines with a few trad climbs, from roughly 5.6 up through 5.11, with most routes in the 5.9 and 5.10 range. A broad ledge about halfway up splits the wall, so many routes can be climbed as two separate pitches or stitched together. The wall sees little traffic and tends to be dirty, so expect some scrubbing. A 60 meter rope reaches the ground from the top, though knotting the ends is wise.

wa_d_main_wall_east.blurb: Main Wall East is the eastern end of the Main Wall on Mt. Erie, on Fidalgo Island. The rock is steep to overhanging and more broken than the west side, darker in colour, and prone to runoff and wet streaks after rain. Climbing here is mostly trad, plus a handful of sport lines. Many of the bolted lines still call for a small set of cams. Grades go from about 5.6 to 5.12, with the bulk in the 5.8 to 5.11 range. A steep gully separates it from the neighbouring Pigeon Stool wall, and the trail can be muddy early in the season or after rain.
